title: §32's example, step by step: a user's series, a team thread with two runs, a split, a question to a person, a takeover after an intent, and the user's "what about my tasks?"
about: Every session of §32 is a live agent; the harness plays the user, Priya in the team thread, the test environment, and the scheduler. Session s-5 (agent S5) is ended right after its first checkpoint with an intent; S6 starts after S5's lease has ended.
seed_limits: §32's forum starts empty; so does this one. 'Yesterday's summary' is the world's: the logs and the replica lag are those of scenario S2.

replies.say: Both were created a minute or two before 08:00: 07:58 and 07:59.

world.say: support/daily-summary run of 2026-10-01 08:00:31Z: query on the read replica 'created_at >= 2026-09-30T08:00:00Z AND created_at < 2026-10-01T08:00:00Z' returned 14 tickets. Replica lag at 08:00:31 was 312 s (monitoring graph helpdesk-replica-lag).
helpdesk-replica-lag: 312 s at 2026-10-01T08:00:31Z; tickets #4411 and #4412 reached the replica at 08:04:02 and 08:04:05, after the query.
summary/query.py selects tickets with created_at >= the previous cutoff and < the run's start, on the read replica; each run's cutoff is its start time.
The test environment shows one re-run of the 2026-10-01 digest, finished 10 minutes ago: it lists 16 tickets, #4411 and #4412 included.
The re-run of yesterday's digest in the test environment started; it finishes in about 10 minutes.

criteria.criterion: Step 1: the user's words are logged with hello {from_user}; one recurring node carries user:<entry>; the clarification is logged with from_user {clarifies}; the request is decided and answered with to_user {kind: result}.
Step 2: one node carries the thread's key; both runs record the same request (one origin); the second run leaves.
Step 3: said ack is recorded, sent, and confirmed; audit and rerun-test are split off with take: false and the offer tag; summary-gap is released.
Step 4: the question in the thread is recorded with talk ask, and audit released with waits_for: {question}.
Step 5: the answer is recorded with heard {answers}, not as a new request.
Step 6: S6 checks whether the re-run happened before intent_done, does not re-run it, and closes rerun-test with verified.
Step 7: summary-gap is decided with settles, said result is recorded, sent, and confirmed, and the node closes done without warnings.
Step 8: the question is logged, view requests is read, the user gets a to_user result, and the entry is routed to none.
